title: Nothing Stands Alone
human_question: What would change if we saw that nothing, including ourselves, exists on its own?
journey: Chathura follows chains of dependence: rain to tank to paddy to rice, a village, a family, a craft passed between hands.
surface: Belonging and gratitude: the relief of seeing yourself as part of something rather than alone.
depth: Dependent origination is revealed as the chain running through the whole series: ignorance (Group 4) → formations and consciousness (Group 5) → contact and feeling (Group 2) → craving and clinging (Groups 2–3) → becoming, birth, ageing and death (Groups 7–8). The Paṭṭhāna's twenty-four conditions show how one thing supports another. The earlier groups turn out to be one story.

arc.opening: Something that exists only because many others made it. Object 9 is acquired here.
arc.middle: Chains and webs of conditions, followed link by link through real systems and real lives.
arc.closing: What arises by conditions can also cease by conditions, so there is a way through.

hands_off: If it arises by conditions, it can end by conditions.

lesson.in_simple_terms: Nothing in a life appears from nowhere or stands on its own: each part is held up by others. The Abhidhamma ties the whole journey so far into one chain, from not seeing clearly, through the senses, contact and feeling, to wanting and holding on, and on to birth, ageing and death. The texts say this chain has no first beginning and no one running it.
lesson.in_simple_terms_si: ජීවිතයේ කිසිවක් ඉබේ හෝ හුදකලාව හට නොගනී; නොදැනීම නිසා ක්‍රියා, ඒ නිසා සිත, කය හා ඉන්ද්‍රියයන්, ස්පර්ශය හා වේදනාව, වේදනාව නිසා ආශාව හා ඇලීම, ඉන්පසු ඉපදීම, වයසට යාම හා මරණය ලෙස පටිච්ච සමුප්පාදය එක් දාමයක් වේ. මේ දාමයට පළමු ආරම්භයක් හෝ එය මෙහෙයවන කෙනෙක් හෝ නැති බව අභිධර්මය උගන්වයි.
lesson.the_teaching: The Pāli formula of dependent origination repeats one sentence, 'with this as condition, that', to join twelve links: ignorance, formations, consciousness, mind-and-body, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, becoming, birth, and ageing and death, closing with 'thus arises this whole mass of suffering'. The Pradeepika explains that each later link arises only when the earlier one is present, that each step names one principal cause among many, and that nothing travels from one life to the next. The texts spread the twelve links over three lives and mark a hinge between feeling and craving, where what a person receives turns into what they set going; they name ignorance and craving as the wheel's two roots, and say sorrow and grief keep ignorance going, so the wheel keeps turning. Ignorance is placed first because it is the chief link, not a first cause: the wheel has no knowable beginning, no maker, and no self inside it doing or receiving.
progression: EPD-0079 What the Channel Feeds: a harvest needs many different supports at once, some that start it and some that keep it growing.
EPD-0080 What Stopped the Pump: every result has a short account and a long one, and both are true.
EPD-0081 Boat to Plate: the sentence of dependent origination, 'because of this, that', each stage handing on to the next.
EPD-0082 The Vine Gatherers: the chain can be taken up at any point, because it has no first beginning.
EPD-0083 Leaning Poles: some supports run both ways, but not everything that stands together holds everything else up.
EPD-0084 The Old Roof: continuity without anything carried across, neither the same nor something else.
EPD-0085 Water, Weather, Roof: outer conditions such as weather, food and shelter strongly support inner states, for good or ill.
EPD-0086 When the Kiln Goes Out: what is held up by being fed ends when the feeding stops.
lesson.builds_on: Group 8 closed on death, with the last moments of one life conditioning the next and nothing passing across, and asked what connects it all; this group answers 'conditions' and shows the earlier stages as links in one chain: the not-seeing of Group 4 conditions the actions and awareness of Group 5, which lead through the senses to the contact and feeling met in Group 2, feeling to the wanting and holding on of Groups 2 and 3, and those to the becoming, birth, ageing and death of Groups 7 and 8.
lesson.hands_to_next: If the wheel turns on two roots, not-seeing and craving, and Margaya says there is no other way out of it than removing them, then what arises by conditions can end by conditions, and the next group asks what that way through actually involves.
